summary: A message steered into a running Claude turn no longer counts as a turn of its own, so the chat stops looking busy for good and a profile switch is no longer refused after steering.

desktop.reason: No renderer change; the existing busy refusal simply stops firing after a finished turn.

reactNativeIos.reason: The phone asks the backend to switch; the count lives in the backend.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as React Native: the count lives in the backend.

storageDataMigration.reason: In-memory count only; nothing stored changes.

updateRelease.reason: Ships with the next desktop release; no wire change.

automated: Unit and WebSocket-boundary tests: three Claude prompts settled by one turn.completed leave the chat switchable; a promoted Claude message releases its count; a tool.started after the result (a late steer run as its own turn) keeps the chat busy until its turn.completed. The first three fail without the fix.
hardware: Diagnosed from the packaged app log on 2026-10-02: chat 71c92391 had six submitUserTurn entries between 08:47 and 08:52 UTC and one turn.completed at 09:09, then every profile switch was refused as busy until an agent switch restarted the session.
notExercised: A live profile switch after steering has not been clicked in a packaged build yet.
A late steer whose own turn uses no tool and only writes text is not re-marked busy, so a switch in that window is not refused by the count; the session status check still applies.
